speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The ARB consists of senior and respected asatizahs in the community.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is how the ARS system should work.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It monitors and takes action to bar those whose views are inimical to social cohesion from preaching.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I wish to assure the Member that ARB and MUIS take ARS registration seriously.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Both MUIS and ARB conduct regular reviews of the ARS system.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ARS is meant to build up and support our asatizah community, so that they are reliable and credible sources of religious knowledge for the Muslim community and play an important role in fostering peace and harmony.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):  : I would like to thank our asatizahs for their hard work in implementing the ARS.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through our collective efforts, we can build a Muslim community together that is strong, confident and constantly able to contribute to our nation's progress.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The asatizahs' support of ARS is a reflection of their commitment to abide by the Code of Ethics that was established according to Islamic values that are durable, progressive and moderate.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is essential in promoting religious harmony within Singapore’s multiracial society.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I have a supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Assuming an asatizah loses his accreditation, is there a process whereby the asatizah can be accredited again?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is not easy for the asatizah to lose his accreditation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He must have been very egregious to have lost it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, the process of getting him on board should not be too easy either.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, the ARB and MUIS will look into how we can bring such asatizahs back to ensure that they do not then regress into the situation when their ARS registration was cancelled in the first place.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps, this might be a useful thing to be made compulsory.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: But knowing the numbers are big, there may be some limitations.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps, the best way to assess a candidate is when you are actually able to encounter them face-to-face, interact with them and look at their non-verbal communication skills.

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Has there been any number that can be reported?

speaker: Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Since 2017, when the ARS scheme came about, has there been any asatizah who has been reported to be doing something negative or inappropriate?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The interviews are conducted on a case-by-case basis because some of the asatizahs come from institutions that we do not know about and the ARB needs to find out more before considering whether to register them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For those who come from established institutions, we are not too worried.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we also do monitor them and we must make sure that we are satisfied that, coming from those institutions, they do not mar the reputation of such institutions by teaching segregationist teachings and so forth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The second question on the face-to-face interview, it is part of that process.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I do take it that the numbers are not extremely difficult to manage, but we have to prioritise.
